To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the kinematics of the molecular outflows are well described by the momentum-conserving model of Shu etal.(1991); (2) the structure of the outflows is well described by the ballistic bow shock model of Raga etal.(1990); (3) the power-law index of MV relationship depends on the viewing angle and the time-variability of the jet or wind; (4) the jet-driven model can explain the observed features of HH 212

the shape and kinematics of a protostellar outflow are primarily determined by the driving mechanism, and that a wind-driven outflow is characterized by a lobe structure in position-velocity diagrams.

(a) the kinematics of the swept-up ambient shell in jet-driven outflows can be described well by a simple ballistic bowshock model, and that (b) the kinematics in wind-driven outflows can also be described well by simple momentum-conserving models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinematic properties of protostellar outflow.
the kinematics of molecular outflows and their relation to the physical properties and driving mechanism of the outflows.
the hydrodynamics of protostellar outflow.

the observed kinematic features of protostellar outflow are consistent with both a jet- and wind-driving mechanism.
both jet-driven and wind-driven models are viable.
both models are viable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinematics of the observed molecular outflows can be explained by either a steady jet or a steady wind.
the jet-driven model can explain the kinematics of outflow lobes in HH objects, while the wind-driven model can explain those in molecular outflows.
the kinematics of the molecular outflows are not a strong constraint on the nature of the driving mechanism.

both the jet- and wind-drives can produce outflows with similar kinematics.
